chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Musa ibn Ukeyl al-Nuymari, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When the owner of the right is pleased with the oath of the denier regarding his right, so he makes him swear, and he swears that there is no right for him against him, the oath removes the right of the claimant, so there is no claim for him.

I said to him, 'And if there was just proof over it?' He said, 'Yes, and even if he establishes after what he made him swear by Allah, fifty oaths, it would not be for him, and the oath had invalidated everything he had claimed before it, from what had been sworn against him.'
ai.seo_question: Does an oath extinguish a claim even if proof is presented later?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the juristic principle of 'radha bi al-yamin', where a claimant's acceptance of the defendant's oath extinguishes the debt, a ruling derived from the Quranic verse on oaths. Notably, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that this extinguishment is absolute, meaning even subsequent production of strong evidence or repeated oaths cannot revive the claim once the initial 'pleasure' with the oath has occurred. This highlights the finality of the oath in Shia jurisprudence as a complete discharge of liability.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazal, from Ali Bin Uqba, from Musa Bin Akeyl Al Numeyri, from Ibn Abu Yafour, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When the owner of the right is happy with the oath which would deny him his right, so the (defendant) swears an oath that there is no right for him (the claimant), the swearing does away with the right of the claimant, so there is no claim for him’.

I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘And if there was just proof over it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, even if he were to establish after what has been sworn by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, sworn endorsements of fifty (men), it would not be for him, and the oath would have invalidated everything what he had claimed for before it, from what has been oathed against him’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn Faddal from Ali ibn ‘Uqbah from Musa ibn ‘Ukayl al-Numayriy from ibn abu Ya’fur who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ’
If a plaintiff agrees with the defendant’s taking an oath who then swears that the plaintiff does not have any right on him, it abolishes the right of the plaintiff and the case is dismissed.’

I then asked, ‘What happens if he can present just testimony?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, even so, an oath by Allah fifty times abolishes and invalidates his claim because of which he had asked for an oath.’”
